label: single host, public weights, warm cache, no fleet claim; all methods lossless; FLOAT_TENSOR and WEIGHT_DELTA were measured at the codec level (per-tensor frames), not through the store planner

environment.zstd: *** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.4, by Yann Collet ***

cases.role: base of the independent fine-tune pair

pairs.note: step0 -> step1 of the same published EleutherAI/pythia-70m training run
step1 -> step2 of the same published training run
step2 -> step4 of the same published training run (two optimizer steps)
step4 -> step8 of the same published training run (four optimizer steps)
Qwen2.5-0.5B base -> Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; a separate instruction-tuning run, not a neighbouring training step

method.float_tensor: modes::encode_float_tensor (mode 9) on every tensor's exact bytes; zstd CLI -19 -T1 and default -3 -T1 on the same per-tensor bytes; whole-file zstd and ZipNN are secondary references
method.weight_delta: weight_delta::encode_weight_delta (mode 11) against the corresponding base tensor's mode-9 frame; base frames are recomputed, never written to disk; the newer checkpoint's own zstd -19 per-tensor total is the independent baseline
method.restore: single-threaded in-process decode, median of 5 reps per tensor; reported totals are the sum of per-tensor medians and exclude storage I/O; zstd frames are the CLI's -19 output decoded with libzstd; delta bytes read include the base mode-9 frame
method.exactness: every FLOAT_TENSOR, WEIGHT_DELTA (both decode routes), and zstd round-trip was byte-compared with the original tensor bytes
method.per_tensor_checkpointing: whole-file independent zstd baselines compress the safetensors header too; per-tensor baselines do not; both are reported

float_tensor.note: FLOAT_TENSOR is a lossless exponent-plane Huffman + raw sign+mantissa coder; it is not a general LZ or a learned coder. pythia-70m step revisions publish F32 weights, not BF16.

patch_from.outcome: killed by the 3 GiB court memory limit (SIGKILL)

float_tensor_bf16.note: FLOAT_TENSOR wins both BF16 Qwen checkpoints against per-tensor zstd -19 and is within 0.06 % of ZipNN 0.5.4 (slightly smaller in this run). All tensors of at least 1 MiB win; only tiny norm/bias tensors lose, by at most a few hundred bytes each.

float_tensor_fp32.note: FLOAT_TENSOR loses all five F32 pythia checkpoints: +62 % versus per-tensor zstd -19 and +95 % versus ZipNN. The published F32 tensors have degenerate low mantissa bytes (probe below), and mode 9 stores sign+mantissa raw, so it cannot remove that redundancy. pythia checkpoints are F32, not BF16 or FP16.

delta_consecutive.note: WEIGHT_DELTA is 5.1-34.1 % of independent per-tensor zstd -19 on the four consecutive pairs, and 2.4-3.3x smaller than the best zstd --patch-from on the three pairs where more than 19 bytes changed. On the step0->step1 pair only 19 bytes differ; there mode 11 loses 246x to --patch-from because every non-constant Huffman plane costs at least one bit per element.

delta_fine_tune.note: The independent fine-tune (97.93 % of BF16 words changed) is 70.50 % of independent zstd -19 and 72.20 % of the best --patch-from. Delta therefore helps the fine-tune, but much less than the meaningful consecutive checkpoints.

separation.note: The two cases are never aggregated. Consecutive checkpoints (excluding the 19-byte step0->step1 artifact) sit at 19.4-34.1 % of zstd -19; the fine-tune sits at 70.5 %. The delta vocabulary is the same; only the amount of change differs.

conclusions.restore: Delta wins bytes but loses decode time: 6.7-12x slower than zstd for FLOAT_TENSOR, 16-21x for the pythia deltas, and 44x for the Qwen fine-tune delta (sum of per-tensor decode medians, single-threaded, excluding storage I/O).
conclusions.corpus_caveat: The published EleutherAI/pythia-70m step0 and step1 files differ in exactly 19 bytes (measured by direct file comparison and by the mode-11 changed-word count). That pair is reported separately and is not used as the headline consecutive-checkpoint result.

reproduce: scripts/docker-court.sh bench 'python3 bench/scripts/real_model_fetch.py --repo EleutherAI/pythia-70m --revision step0 --file model.safetensors --dest .docker-cache/real-corpus/pythia-70m-step0.safetensors'
residual_risks: all timings are single-host, warm-cache, inside one bench court; every read is lens-cached by the host page cache (no cache-drop capability)
restore totals are sums of per-tensor medians and exclude storage I/O; they are not a single wall-clock pass
ZipNN is run whole-file only and is not delta-aware; the fine-tune comparison is against that independent configuration
mode 9 / mode 11 are measured as codec frames; the shipped store planner also prices raw, zstd, and semantic delta per tensor and may choose differently
